title: The three-minute Caravan film of 1952
summary: Willard describes a jukebox short of Caravan with Tizol's solo; Rose thinks he may not have known it was filmed.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Here is another short called 'Caravan,' three minutes long. It was probably one of those -- yeah, made by Snyder. They made them for those visual jukeboxes, a little film that would go on when you put your money in, and apparently, they did 'Caravan.' It says 'Duke Ellington and his orchestra played the title number with solo by Juan Tizol, trombone, and featuring Jimmy Hamilton, Willie Smith, Russell Procope, Paul Gonzalves, Harry Carney, Ray Nance, Willie Cook, Cat Anderson, Britt Woodman, Quentin Jackson, and Louie Bellson.' Do you remember that? That was 1952. A little while after Louie joined, right?
Yeah. He was in the band doing it, and probably didn't even know they were doing it.
